Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the full scope of the module by listing all topics covered—including HTML form structure, input types, accessibility with labels and fieldsets, and form submission—serving as a navigation guide for learners and a planning reference for instructors.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A topic outline covering HTML form fundamentals—including form structure, user input elements, and data submission—that learners use to preview the key concepts addressed in the module and instructors use to confirm curricular scope.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to HTML Forms
Artifacts.Description: A foundational reading that explains what HTML forms are, why they matter, and how the core form element structures user input and data submission, intended for learners to read before studying specific form components.

Artifacts.Name: Form Input Types and Elements
Artifacts.Description: A reading that surveys the full range of HTML input types and form elements (text, email, checkbox, select, etc.), helping learners understand which element to choose based on the kind of data being collected.

Artifacts.Name: Labels, Fieldsets, and Form Accessibility
Artifacts.Description: A reading covering how to use label elements, fieldsets, and legends to make forms accessible to all users, including those using assistive technologies, so learners can build inclusive form interfaces.

Artifacts.Name: Form Submission and Action Attributes
Artifacts.Description: A reading explaining the action, method, and enctype attributes on the form element that control where and how submitted data is sent, helping learners understand the mechanics of form submission.

Artifacts.Name: Built-in HTML5 Validation Attributes
Artifacts.Description: A reading that introduces HTML5's built-in validation attributes (required, pattern, min, max, minlength, etc.) and explains how to enforce input rules directly in markup without JavaScript.

Artifacts.Name: Custom JavaScript Form Validation
Artifacts.Description: A reading that goes beyond HTML5 built-in validation to cover writing custom JavaScript validation logic, including cross-field comparisons and dynamic error handling for real-world form requirements.

Artifacts.Name: Validation Feedback and User Experience
Artifacts.Description: A reading focused on best practices for presenting validation error messages and feedback in ways that are clear, timely, and user-friendly, helping learners design forms that guide users to successful submission.
